title: Choose the key
prompt: To group words that are anagrams of each other, the HashMap key should be…
options: The word's letters sorted (`"tea"` → `"aet"`) — identical for all anagrams
explanation: A good grouping key is a canonical form: something equal for exactly the items that belong together. Length or first letter collide for non-anagrams. (A 26-count signature also works.)

title: Drill: count equal pairs
prompt: From memory: return the number of pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `nums[i] == nums[j]`. One pass: for each element, the pairs it completes = how many copies came before it. Read the count, add to answer, then increment the count — the counting idiom with a twist.

solution.explanation: Each x pairs with every earlier copy of itself, so adding the count BEFORE recording x counts each pair exactly once (i < j). Same check-then-record ordering as Two Sum. O(n) time, O(n) space.

hints: When you reach a value x, how many new pairs does it complete? Only the copies that came before it.
Keep a running count per value; add the current count to the answer before incrementing it.

title: Drill: any pair sums to target
prompt: From memory (the complement move): return whether any two distinct elements of `nums` add up to `target`. Use a HashSet of seen values, checking the complement before inserting.

solution.explanation: The partner of x is `target - x`; a HashSet of earlier values answers "have I seen it?" in O(1). Checking before inserting means a single 3 with target 6 is not matched with itself, while `[3,3]` still works. O(n) time, O(n) space.

hints: For each x, exactly one other value would complete the pair. What is it?
Remember every value you have already passed in a set, and look the partner up.
Check `seen.contains(target - x)` BEFORE `seen.add(x)`, so x never pairs with itself.

title: Template recall: group by sorted key
prompt: From memory: complete the Group Anagrams grouping template (sorted `char[]` key + `computeIfAbsent`).
explanation: Sorting the letters gives a canonical key shared by exactly the anagrams. `computeIfAbsent` creates the list on first sight and returns it either way, so `.add(w)` always works; `values()` is the collection of groups.

title: Drill: prefix products (exclusive)
prompt:
From memory: return `out` where `out[i]` is the product of every element **before** index `i` (`out[0] = 1`). One pass with a running product — this is the first half of Product of Array Except Self.

`[1,2,3,4]` → `[1,1,2,6]`

tests.note: a zero wipes everything after it

solution.explanation: Write the running product into `out[i]` before multiplying `nums[i]` in — that ordering is what excludes index i. Run the same loop right-to-left and multiply, and you have Product of Array Except Self. O(n) time, O(n) output space.

hints: out[i+1] differs from out[i] by exactly one factor. Which one?
Keep a running product starting at 1 and walk left to right.
Order matters: `out[i] = running;` first, then `running *= nums[i];`.
